abstract: This paper examines how far-right political actors used AI-generated multimedia content in their digital campaigns during the 2024 European Parliament elections, focusing on the platforms Instagram and X. It situates the analysis at the intersection of populist communication strategies and emerging generative AI technologies. The study explores how synthetic images and other AI-produced media serve populist messaging and campaigning practices.
key_claims: Far-right actors incorporated AI-generated multimedia content into their digital campaigning during the 2024 European elections.
The convergence of populism and generative AI represents a notable development in contemporary political communication.
Platform affordances of Instagram and X shape how AI-generated content is deployed in far-right campaigns.
methods: Analysis of political content posted on Instagram and X during the 2024 European Parliament election campaign.
Focus on far-right actors' use of AI-generated multimedia (specific methodological details not available from the abstract alone).
findings: Specific empirical findings are not available from the abstract; the paper reports on the presence and use of AI-generated multimedia in far-right digital campaigning across the two platforms.
contributions: Provides an empirical case study of AI-generated content in far-right electoral communication within the European context.
Connects scholarship on populist digital campaigning with the emerging phenomenon of generative AI in politics.
Offers a comparative view across two major social media platforms (Instagram and X).
framing: The paper positions itself within research on populist and far-right digital communication, extending that conversation to address the implications of generative artificial intelligence for electoral campaigning in the European Union.
